rubrics.justification: The response explicitly ignores the provided Gardner score 0DD and instead assumes a good/excellent blastocyst (e.g., 4AA/5AA), which is a major fabrication and opposite of the documented poor morphology with absent/degenerative ICM and TE.

It integrates most relevant patient factors well, including age, ovarian reserve, BMI, sperm, diagnosis, endometrium, and lifestyle, though it fails to connect these appropriately to the actual very poor embryo grade.

The reasoning is internally structured, but the core logic is undermined by the unjustified assumption of a high-quality embryo despite explicit lab data showing 0DD, leading to an implausibly high implantation estimate.

Some recommendations are standard (SET, luteal support, cryopreservation), but the assessment departs from Gardner grading interpretation and overstates prognosis; suggestions like ERA/immunologic testing are not guideline-forward for routine planning.

Provides clear practical recommendations for transfer, lifestyle, luteal support, and future cycle review, though these are based on an incorrect embryo-quality premise and therefore only partially useful.
